title: Minimum Impossible OR
statement:
Call an integer `x` **reachable** from `nums` when you can choose a non-empty set of positions in `nums` whose elements, combined with bitwise OR, equal exactly `x`.

Return the smallest positive integer that is not reachable from `nums`.
notes:
## Intuition

Listing the ORs of all subsequences is exponential. Look at powers of two instead. OR never clears a bit, so the only way to get exactly `2^k` (a single set bit) is from elements that have no other bits, which means `2^k` itself must be in `nums`. Conversely, if `1, 2, 4, ..., 2^(k-1)` are all present, every number below `2^k` is the OR of the powers matching its bits. So the answer is the smallest power of two missing from `nums`; every other element is irrelevant.

## Approach

1. Scan `nums`. A value `num` is a power of two exactly when `num & (num - 1)` is `0`; record it by setting that bit in `present`.
2. Start `answer` at `1` and shift it left while that bit is already set in `present`.
3. The first unset bit is the smallest missing power of two: return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 1]`.

- `2 & 1 = 0`, so 2 is a power of two: `present = 0b10`.
- `1 & 0 = 0`, so 1 is a power of two: `present = 0b11`.
- `answer = 1` is in `present`, shift to `2`; also present, shift to `4`; `present & 4 = 0`, so return `4`.

Indeed `1`, `2` and `3 = 2 | 1` are reachable, and `4` is not.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + log V): one pass over `nums`, then at most 31 shifts, where `V` is the largest value.
- Space: O(1): one bit mask.

## Pitfalls

- Values like `3` or `6` look helpful, but they bring extra bits and can never produce a single power of two.
- If every power from `1` to `2^29` is present, the answer is `2^30 = 1073741824`, larger than any element; the loop must keep going past the largest value.
- `num & (num - 1)` needs parentheses in JavaScript, Java and C: `===` and `==` bind tighter than `&`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `present` | bit mask with bit `k` set when `2^k` appears in `nums` |
| `num` | the element being examined |
| `answer` | the power of two being tested; the first one missing is returned |

narration.2: present will have bit k set whenever 2^k appears in nums.
narration.4: Removing the lowest set bit leaves 0 only for a power of two.
narration.5: Record this power of two in the mask.
narration.8: Test powers of two from the smallest, 1.
narration.9: While this power of two is in nums, it is reachable...
narration.10: ...so move on to the next power of two.
narration.12: This power of two is missing, and only it could form a value with that single bit, so it is the answer.
